analysis: Both units are patch hunks of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a test-vector fixture. The visible changes only replace prompt_contract_id values (per-model and per-case plan) and the derived block-boundary chain_hash and last_complete_block_hash values. The fixture covers the models gpt-oss-style (token 200006), qwen3.5-35b-a3b and qwen3.6-35b-a3b-vl-mtp-mxfp8. The replacements are consistent in the visible hunks: every old ID maps to a single new ID within each model, and every chain_hash change sits next to a contract ID change, as expected when the contract ID seeds the chain hashes. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key-handling, or routing logic is visible in this batch. The relevant surface is the cache-routing and prefix-cache area (T-041). Changed contract IDs and chain hashes alter the cache-isolation namespace and the cross-tenant sharing behavior only if the unseen Swift or Go implementations produce different values from these vectors. The producing implementation change (likely a prompt-contract version or template change) is not in this batch, so I cannot verify that the vectors match the implementation. Excerpts are truncated and range_map_complete=false, so only visible hunks were checked. Integration should confirm the contract-derivation code change and that provider and coordinator cross-language golden tests agree, so that cache routing does not silently diverge. No concrete security regression is evidenced here.
